items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: And so it took me a little while to get used to that because the man had great musicians in his band, and Jo Jones was there

ctx.x: And so now, what do you see was the difference between the way you all were playing and the way Basie's band played?

Well, Basie was a smoothie, natural swinger. I mean a natural swinger. And so it took me a little while to get used to that because the man had great musicians in his band, and Jo Jones was there, and that little rascal, as I told you before, he revolutionized drums to me.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: A lot of times they used to ask me to do recordings and I'd say, 'Send for Crawford. I'm not going to play these 4 bars. I don't know how to play them yet. Send for Crawford to play these 4 bars and I'll finish the date...'

ctx.x: Who played drums in that band, in the Bennie Moten band?

Mac Washington. Looked somewhat like Jimmie Crawford but very beautiful. What they used to call, they call bombs now, stumbles - he made stumbles. He made that connection from the interlude to the... - nobody could drop in the bucket like him. A lot of times they used to ask me to do recordings and I'd say, "Send for Crawford. I'm not going to play these 4 bars. I don't know how to play them yet. Send for Crawford to play these 4 bars and I'll finish the date... Because he knew how to play dum - de dum - de dum -…
